meta.titre: Meat and Fish Cookery: Choosing, Tenderising and Cooking
meta.sous_theme: Structure of meat, groups of fish, choice and cooking methods

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: At a roadside in Douala, fish is grilled over charcoal while a butcher nearby cuts beef for the day's customers. Meat and fish are the main body-building foods in many homes, yet they are costly and are easily spoilt by poor choice or wrong cooking. The GCE asks you to classify them, to choose them well, and to explain why some meat stays tough.

items: Protein builds and repairs the body.
Stewing and boiling are moist methods; grilling and roasting are dry methods.
Bacteria grow quickly in warm, moist, protein-rich food.

sections.titre: Meat and fish: structure, choice and cooking
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meat
Meat is made of muscle fibres (the lean part), connective tissue and fat. Meat is tough when it has long, thick fibres and a lot of connective tissue. This is found in older animals and in muscles that work hard, such as the neck and leg. Tender meat comes from young animals and from muscles that do little work.

| Type of cut | Best methods |
|---|---|
| Tender cuts | grilling, frying, roasting (short cooking time) |
| Tough cuts | stewing, boiling, braising (long, slow, moist cooking) |

Slow cooking in moisture changes the collagen of the connective tissue into gelatine, so the meat softens. Meat can also be made tender by cutting it across the fibres, mincing, beating, or marinating it in an acid such as lemon juice or vinegar, or with a fruit that contains a protein-softening enzyme such as pawpaw.

**Offals** are the edible internal organs and some other parts of an animal. Examples: liver, kidney, heart, tongue and tripe. Liver is rich in iron and vitamin A. Offals are cheap but spoil quickly, so they must be cooked soon after buying.

### Fish
Fish is classified into three groups.

| Group | Features | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| White fish | little fat in the flesh; oil kept in the liver | cod, hake |
| Oily fish | oil spread through the flesh; source of vitamins A and D | mackerel, herring, sardines |
| Shellfish | a hard shell; crustaceans and molluscs | prawns, crabs, crayfish, oysters |

**Fresh fish** has bright, full, clear eyes, red gills, firm elastic flesh, shiny scales and a fresh smell. Fish has short fibres and little connective tissue, so it cooks quickly and breaks easily; overcooking makes it dry. Fish is cooked by grilling, frying, steaming, poaching or baking, and spoils faster than meat.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked why a piece of meat is tough or how to make it tender.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the cause and then the remedy. Causes: age of the animal, muscles that work hard, and the amount of connective tissue. Remedies: long slow moist cooking, cutting across the fibres, mincing, beating with a mallet, marinating in acid, and using a protein-softening enzyme from pawpaw. Always explain how the remedy works, for example that moist heat turns collagen to gelatine.

variantes.nom: Choosing and storing meat and fish
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for points to look for when buying, or for rules of hygiene.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Buy from a clean seller. Fresh meat has a good colour, is firm and has no unpleasant smell. Choose fish with bright full eyes, red gills and firm flesh. Keep raw meat and fish cold, covered and away from cooked food so that bacteria do not spread, and cook or freeze them quickly. Wash hands, knives and boards after handling raw meat or fish.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain why a piece of beef from the leg of an old cow is tougher than a piece from a young calf, and describe how the tough meat can be made tender. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Explain" asks for reasons, and "describe" asks for methods with a short account of how they work. Six marks suggest three points in each part.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Part 1: three reasons. Part 2: three methods with how they work.

etapes.justification: Toughness comes from the structure of the meat.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. An old animal has more connective tissue. 2. The muscle fibres are longer and thicker. 3. A leg muscle works hard and so is firmer than meat from a muscle that works little.

etapes.justification: Moist heat acts on the connective tissue.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Stew or boil slowly in liquid with a lid: the collagen changes into gelatine and the meat softens.

etapes.justification: These break fibres or soften protein.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Cut across the fibres or mince the meat to shorten the fibres; marinate in lemon juice or vinegar, or use pawpaw, which contains an enzyme that softens protein.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Reasons:** the old animal's meat has more connective tissue, longer and thicker fibres, and the leg muscle works hard. **Tenderising:** (1) cook slowly in moist heat, so collagen turns to gelatine; (2) cut across the fibres or mince the meat, which shortens the fibres; (3) marinate in an acid such as lemon juice or use pawpaw, whose enzyme softens protein.

items.erreur_markdown: Classing fish as freshwater fish and sea fish.
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes where the fish lives. For cookery, fish is classed by its flesh and shell: white fish, oily fish and shellfish.
items.correction_markdown: Name the three groups and give an example of each.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that a tough cut should be fried quickly over a high heat to make it tender.
items.pourquoi_faux: Short, dry cooking hardens the fibres of a tough cut. Tenderness comes from slow, moist cooking.
items.correction_markdown: Stew, boil or braise tough cuts; keep grilling and frying for tender cuts.

items.erreur_markdown: Defining offals as the bones and waste thrown away after cutting a carcass.
items.pourquoi_faux: Offals are edible internal organs and other parts, such as liver and kidney, and they are eaten.
items.correction_markdown: Offals are edible internal organs and parts of an animal. Examples: liver, kidney, heart and tongue.

items.erreur_markdown: Cooking fish for a long time like tough beef to make sure it is done.
items.pourquoi_faux: Fish has short fibres and little connective tissue, so it cooks quickly; a long time makes it dry and makes it break up.
items.correction_markdown: Cook fish gently for a short time until the flesh is firm and flakes easily.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that fresh fish has a strong smell, sunken eyes and soft flesh.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are signs of stale fish. Fresh fish has bright, full eyes, red gills, firm flesh and a fresh smell.
items.correction_markdown: Quote the opposite signs: bright full eyes, red gills, firm flesh, shiny scales.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Give the group of fish to which each belongs: cod, mackerel, prawn, oyster. (b) State three examples of offals.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Cod: **white fish**. Mackerel: **oily fish**. Prawn: **shellfish** (crustacean). Oyster: **shellfish** (mollusc). (b) Any three of: liver, kidney, heart, tongue, tripe.

items.enonce_markdown: Beef costs $3\,200$ FCFA per kilogram and fish costs $2\,000$ FCFA per kilogram (assumed prices). A family of eight is deciding between 1.5 kg of beef and 2 kg of fish for one meal. (a) Find the cost of each. (b) Find the cost per person for each. (c) How much does the family save in all by buying the fish?

Mrs Ngu buys a fish and some beef from the market. (a) State four signs she should check to be sure the fish is fresh. (b) Explain why she stews the tough beef slowly with the lid on, but cooks fish fillets for only a short time. (c) Explain why raw meat should be stored apart from cooked food.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Any four of: bright, clear, full eyes; red gills; firm elastic flesh; shiny scales; fresh smell. (b) Beef has much connective tissue which needs long, slow, moist cooking to turn collagen into gelatine; the lid keeps in moisture. Fish has short fibres and little connective tissue, so it is cooked in a short time and long cooking would make it dry and break it. (c) Raw meat may carry harmful bacteria which can pass to cooked food by contact or dripping, and cooked food is eaten without more cooking, so food poisoning could follow.

items_markdown: Tough meat comes from old animals and hard-worked muscles with much connective tissue; tender cuts suit grilling and frying, tough cuts suit stewing and boiling.
Moist heat changes collagen to gelatine; other tenderising ways: cutting across the fibres, mincing, beating, marinating in acid, pawpaw.
Offals are edible internal organs and parts such as liver, kidney, heart, tongue and tripe.
Fish groups: white fish, oily fish, shellfish; know one example of each.
Fresh fish: bright full eyes, red gills, firm flesh, shiny scales, fresh smell; cook it quickly and gently.
Store raw meat and fish cold, covered and apart from cooked food.
